title: Small intestine wall: villi, crypts and enteric nerves
description: Map villus–crypt renewal, epithelial cell types, capillaries and lacteals, plus two enteric nerve plexuses.

questions.question: What are the layers of the small intestinal wall?
questions.answer: From lumen outward they include mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa and serosa or adventitia depending on the segment.

questions.question: What do intestinal villi and crypts do?
questions.answer: Villi expand the absorptive surface. Crypts contain renewing epithelial cells and other specialized cells that help maintain the mucosa.

questions.question: What is the villus?
questions.answer: Fingerlike projection of small-intestinal mucosa with epithelial cover and lamina propria core. Function: Expands absorptive surface.

questions.question: Where is the enterocyte located?
questions.answer: Absorptive columnar epithelial cell with apical microvilli. Function: Takes up digested nutrients.

questions.question: What is the function of the goblet cell?
questions.answer: Function: Lubricates and helps protect mucosal surface. Mucin-producing epithelial cell scattered among enterocytes.
